title: The Census Takers
text: Two blank-faced clerks with ledgers stop the party at a crossing, pens raised, smooth heads tilted. Everyone in the city must be counted, they say in one voice. They would like your names. Behind them, the ledger's pages are thick with names in every hand.

options.label: Give your true names, and let the city count you.

outcomes.text: They write the names down with care, in a hand that is not theirs. Now the city knows you, and it will not forget.

options.label: The craftiest gives false names for everyone, and hopes the city never checks.

outcomes.text: They write the false names down. Somewhere a ledger now lists people who never were, and the city will go looking for them.
They write the names down, then look up. Neither has a face to look up with, yet still they look.

options.label: Snatch their ledger, and see what names it holds.

outcomes.text: Every blank mouth in the city screams at once. It comes for the names you took.
